findings.evidence: The theorem at line 222 requires hψ : ψ.IsPrimitive; it does not establish existence. For F₃ and target ℝ, the trivial character exists but no primitive additive character does.
findings.fix: State that a primitive ψ must be supplied and that coefficients are unique relative to this fixed ψ.
findings.issue: The module overview (lines 38–40, 68–70) and existsUnique_eq_superdiagonalChar docstring (219–221) promise a primitive ψ for every finite commutative ring and RCLike target.

findings.evidence: diagGL_mul_mul_inv_apply (59–62) and superdiagonalHom_diagGLConj (108–112) explicitly place x between the units. Taking tᵢ = tⱼ noncentral makes the advertised factor 1 while conjugation can change x.
findings.fix: Describe the two-sided operation x ↦ tᵢ x tⱼ⁻¹; restrict the scalar-factor and root-value interpretation to commutative R.
findings.issue: The module text (19–25, 34–35) and docstrings at 58, 99 and 107 describe multiplication by tᵢtⱼ⁻¹, although R is allowed to be noncommutative.

summary: The documentation overstates primitive-character existence and describes noncommutative conjugation as scalar multiplication.
